newsitem.title: USA: Zaire needs economic reforms - Belgium's Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: Zaire needs economic reforms - Belgium's Maystadt.

text.p: Zaire will need to implement long-term economic reforms if its creditors are to ease the burden of its foreign debt, Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Saturday.
"We hope that the new government would engage in a durable program of reforms which might allow all creditors to help Zaire," he told reporters.
"We need evidence a new Zaire government is clearly committed to the necessary reforms," he added.
Maystadt was speaking during the semi-annual meeting of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Washington, where he chairs the IMF's policy-making interim committee.
He had been asked what he thought the Zaire conflict meant for its own and other African economies, which the IMF and World Bank are now trying to help with a new debt relief initiative.
Zaire in theory would be eligible to benefit from the initiative if it brought its civil war to an end and implemented economic reforms.
Rebels seeking to oust Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko have overrun around two-thirds of the country.
Earlier this week the IMF and World Bank approved debt relief for Uganda, the first to benefit from an initiative meant to help some 15 to 20 poor countries, mostly in Africa.
